joka.name: Joka
joka.about:
Joka sits at the southern edge of Kolkata, at the point where the municipal corporation area ends. Thakurpukur lies to its north and Pailan to its south, with Asuti and Maheshtala on the west and Nepalgunge and Rania on the east, and it is counted as part of the wider Behala region. Diamond Harbour Road is its main link with the city, while Bakhrahat Road leads out to the towns and villages of South 24 Parganas. The old tram depot has closed, and in recent years new apartment complexes and shops have come up beside the older houses.

Joka is the southern terminus of the Purple Line, and the line's car shed is here too. Trains run north through Thakurpukur, Sakherbazar and Behala Chowrasta to Majerhat, so a tutor who lives anywhere along the line can arrive by metro; check the current timetable before fixing a weekend class.

Gated complexes keep a visitor register, so pass on the tutor's name, tower and flat number before the demo. Older houses on the lanes are a straight doorstep call. Because Joka is the last stop, tutors often fit it at the start or end of their round, so a late-afternoon slot is easy to agree. NXTutors lists tutors living in or near Joka first, then the rest of the zone and online tutors, and the first class is free.

sarsuna.name: Sarsuna
sarsuna.about:
Sarsuna lies on the south-western fringe of Kolkata, with Barisha to the east and Maheshtala to the west, and marks the edge of the municipal corporation area on that side. It is made up of many small paras, among them Sonamukhi and Kashthadanga, stretching from Shakuntala Park to Raidighi. Settlement here goes back to the late eighteenth century, and the area grew quickly after 1947 and again after 1971, when families from across the eastern border settled here and made it their home.

Housing mixes older homes in the paras with planned estates. The West Bengal Housing Board's Sarsuna Satellite Township, where allotments began in 1985, combines plots, ready-built houses and four-storey apartment blocks, and a second satellite township grew up at Shakuntala Park. Sarsuna has no station of its own: the Purple Line stops on Diamond Harbour Road in neighbouring Barisha, such as Sakherbazar and Behala Chowrasta, are the nearest metro, with an auto or bus for the final stretch.

Inside the township a tutor generally walks straight up to the house or flat, and only a few apartment blocks ask visitors to sign in. An after-school weekday slot or a Saturday morning suits most families. NXTutors shows home tutors from Sarsuna, Barisha and Behala first, adds online tutors for specialist subjects, and the first class with each tutor is a free demo.

barisha.name: Barisha
barisha.about:
Barisha is an old residential part of south-west Kolkata, divided into Paschim (west) Barisha and Purba (east) Barisha. It takes in Behala Chowrasta, Janakalyan, Silpara and Sakherbazar and runs up to Thakurpukur. Behala Manton is to the north, Joka to the south, Sarsuna and Dakshin Behala to the west, and Haridevpur, Siriti and Tollygunge to the east. Its heritage runs deep: a family Durga Puja here dates from 1610, and the Barisha Chandi Mela, a local fair, has been held every year since 1792.

Homes are a blend of old family houses on the inner lanes and apartment buildings along the main roads, with newer projects still being added. The Purple Line runs right through the locality, with Sakherbazar and Behala Chowrasta stations on Diamond Harbour Road, which makes Barisha one of the simpler parts of the Behala side to reach by metro.

In the older houses a tutor comes straight to the door; buildings with a caretaker may ask for a name first. Weekday evenings after school and Saturday mornings are the slots families pick most, and lessons often pause for Puja week, so agree that calendar at the start. NXTutors lists tutors living in and around Barisha first, then online tutors, with a free first class.

haridevpur.name: Haridevpur
haridevpur.about:
Haridevpur is a locality on the Tollygunge side of the Behala region, set just off the main road that links Thakurpukur and Joka with Tollygunge. It spans municipal wards 122, 143 and 144, has its own police station in the South West division, and touches Barisha on its western side. Most homes are flats in low and mid-rise apartment buildings, with independent houses on the side streets.

Mahanayak Uttam Kumar station on the Blue Line, at Tollygunge, is the nearest metro stop, and Tollygunge also has a station on the Budge Budge suburban line. Many bus and minibus routes run along the main road towards Thakurpukur and Joka, so a tutor from Tollygunge, Behala or Jadavpur normally needs no more than one change to get here.

Small apartment buildings mean a tutor usually goes straight up to the flat; a few newer blocks keep a register at the entrance, so share the flat number in advance. A slot soon after school, or a weekend morning, is the usual pattern. Because Haridevpur sits between two zones, tutors from both the Tollygunge and Behala sides can be offered. NXTutors lists the nearest first and adds online tutors, and the first class is free.

park-circus.name: Park Circus
park-circus.about:
Park Circus is a central neighbourhood on the northern side of the Ballygunge area. Entally and Sealdah lie to its north, Park Street and Chowringhee to its west, Taltala to the north-west, Tangra to the north-east, Topsia to the east and Ballygunge to the south. It spreads across several municipal wards, connects directly with Park Street, and Park Circus Ground is its most familiar open space. Residential streets sit beside shops and offices, and apartment buildings, older and newer, make up most of the housing.

Park Circus station on the Sealdah South suburban lines, between Sealdah and Ballygunge Junction, serves the area, and Rabindra Sadan on the Blue Line is the nearest metro to the west. The Park Circus Connector runs east to the EM Bypass, where Ritwik Ghatak and VIP Bazar stations on the Orange Line have been open since August 2025, so tutors from Kasba, Garia or Salt Lake have a direct way in.

Buildings with a security desk will ask for the tutor's name, while older houses in the side lanes are a doorstep visit. Families here often prefer an early-evening weekday lesson. NXTutors lists home tutors from Park Circus and the rest of the Ballygunge, Gariahat & Alipore zone first, offers online tutors too, and the first class is a free demo.

southern-avenue.name: Southern Avenue
southern-avenue.about:
Southern Avenue is both a road and the residential quarter around it in the Ballygunge area of South Kolkata. The avenue runs from Gariahat Road in the east to the Kalighat side in the west, linking Golpark with Kalighat, and it is anchored by Rabindra Sarobar, the large artificial lake, with Lake Road and Keyatala Road among the streets that branch off it. The road has an official newer name, but almost everyone still calls it Southern Avenue.

Housing along the avenue and its side roads is a mix of private bungalows and tall apartment buildings. Kalighat on the Blue Line is the nearest metro station, and Ballygunge Junction on the Sealdah South suburban lines lies to the east beyond Gariahat. Tutors coming from Tollygunge, Garia or north Kolkata can therefore use the metro and walk or take an auto for the last stretch.

Bungalows are a doorstep visit; the high-rise buildings have a desk or intercom, so give the tutor's name and flat number in advance. Weekday evenings after school, or a weekend morning, are the slots most families here prefer. NXTutors lists tutors in the Ballygunge, Gariahat & Alipore zone first, then the wider city and online tutors, with a free demo class.

bijoygarh.name: Bijoygarh
bijoygarh.about:
Bijoygarh is a neighbourhood in the southern part of Kolkata, sharing its boundaries with Jadavpur, Baghajatin, Bikramgarh, Regent Estate and Ranikuthi. It began as one of the colonies set up by families who arrived from East Pakistan after 1947; by 1949 the Jadavpur area held about forty such colonies, Bijoygarh among them. Today it is part of Borough X of the municipal corporation, covering wards 95 to 99.

The colony was laid out in house plots, so many streets still have family houses, and apartment buildings have since replaced some of them. Jadavpur and Baghajatin stations on the Sealdah South suburban lines are the nearest railway stops, and Mahanayak Uttam Kumar on the Blue Line is the metro station usually given for the area. Tutors from Jadavpur, Tollygunge and Garia can reach it with one change.

A family house means the tutor walks straight to the door, while apartment buildings may want a name at the gate. Lessons after school on weekdays, or on a Sunday morning, suit most homes here. NXTutors lists home tutors from Bijoygarh and the rest of the Tollygunge, Jadavpur & Garia zone first, then online tutors, and the first class is a free demo.

tiljala.name: Tiljala
tiljala.about:
Tiljala is an east Kolkata neighbourhood with the EM Bypass on its eastern side, Ballygunge to the west, Kasba to the south and Topsia to the north. It was one of the villages the East India Company first rented in 1717 and bought in 1758, and it lay beyond the old Maratha Ditch as a suburb before the city grew around it. Bengali, Marwari, Punjabi, Anglo-Indian and Nepali families all live here, and Picnic Garden Road is one of its main streets.

Housing ranges from older buildings along the market lanes to newer apartment complexes towards the bypass. Ballygunge Junction and Park Circus on the Sealdah South suburban lines are the nearest railway stations, and since August 2025 VIP Bazar and Ritwik Ghatak stations on the Orange Line have served the bypass side, linking Tiljala with Kasba, Mukundapur and Garia.

In the older lanes a tutor goes to the door directly; the complexes near the bypass ask visitors to register, so share the tutor's name ahead of the demo. Families mixing languages at home sometimes ask for a tutor who can explain in Bengali or Hindi, which is worth noting in the request. NXTutors lists nearby tutors first and online tutors next, with a free first class.

topsia.name: Topsia
topsia.about:
Topsia is an east Kolkata neighbourhood beside the junction of the Park Circus Connector and the EM Bypass, falling mainly in municipal ward 66. Park Circus lies to its west and Tiljala to its south. Like its neighbours it was one of the villages known together as Dihi Panchannagram, bought by the East India Company in 1758, and later drew workers from Bihar and Uttar Pradesh to the tanneries and factories nearby.

The area has changed a great deal: tall residential towers now rise near the bypass, among the highest in the city, while older streets keep their low buildings and workshops. The Orange Line station once called Topsia, now Ritwik Ghatak, opened in August 2025 and links the area with Kasba, Mukundapur and Garia. Park Circus on the Sealdah South suburban lines is the nearest railway station, and the Basanti Highway begins here.

In the towers a tutor checks in at the lobby desk and waits for approval from the flat, so tell security in advance. On the older streets the visit is to the door. A weekday slot after school is the usual choice. NXTutors offers home tutors from Topsia and the Kasba & EM Bypass South zone first, then online tutors, and the first class with each is free.

anandapur.name: Anandapur
anandapur.about:
Anandapur lies at the south-eastern fringe of Kolkata and marks the limit of the municipal corporation area on that side, in ward 108. Anandapur Main Road joins the EM Bypass, and Anandapur High Road runs on towards Kalikapur, Adarsh Nagar and Bantala. The locality has its own police station in the East division, and large gated apartment complexes with high-rise towers have come up here over the last two decades.

Hemanta Mukhopadhyay station on the Orange Line, at the Ruby crossing on the bypass, is the nearest metro stop and has been open since March 2024. Ballygunge Junction on the Sealdah South suburban lines is the nearest railway station, and several bus routes link Anandapur with Garia, Ballygunge and the city centre.

Most visits here are to gated complexes, so pre-register the tutor with the security office and share the tower and flat number. Families commonly book a slot after school on weekdays, and many Class 11–12 students add an online session for a specialist subject. NXTutors suggests the nearest home tutors first, then online tutors, and the first class with each is a free demo.

haltu.name: Haltu
haltu.about:
Haltu is a mainly residential neighbourhood of South Kolkata, surrounded by Kasba, Jadavpur, Dhakuria, Kalikapur and Selimpur. It spreads across municipal wards 104 to 109, and Garfa Main Road and Kalikapur Road cross at its centre, with the bus network running through both. Homes are mostly in apartment buildings, older ones on the inner roads and newer ones towards the EM Bypass, with many new projects in recent years.

Three suburban stations are within reach: Ballygunge Junction, Dhakuria and Jadavpur, all on the Sealdah South lines. On the bypass side, Kavi Sukanta station on the Orange Line, at Kalikapur, has been open since March 2024. That puts Haltu within reach of tutors from both the railway side, such as Jadavpur and Dhakuria, and the bypass side, such as Mukundapur and Garia.

In smaller buildings a tutor rings the bell and goes up; newer complexes may ask for a name at the gate. An after-school weekday lesson or a Saturday slot suits most families here. NXTutors lists home tutors who live in or around Haltu first, then the rest of the Kasba & EM Bypass South zone and online tutors, and the first class is a free demo.

survey-park.name: Survey Park
survey-park.about:
Survey Park is a residential locality in the Santoshpur area of south-east Kolkata, close to the EM Bypass and next to Santoshpur, Chak Garia and Ajoy Nagar. It falls in municipal ward 109. Its police station was created in 2011, when several stations in this belt moved from South 24 Parganas to Kolkata Police and most were split into two. Homes are mainly apartment buildings, older blocks on the inner roads and newer ones near the bypass.

Two Orange Line stations on the EM Bypass serve the locality: Jyotirindra Nandi, at Mukundapur, and Satyajit Ray, at Panchasayar, both open since March 2024. The line runs north along the bypass to Kalikapur, the Ruby crossing and Beleghata, and south to Kavi Subhash at New Garia, so a tutor from Kasba, Garia or the bypass side can arrive by metro and finish with a short auto ride.

Most apartment buildings here are small, so a tutor goes straight up; the larger complexes keep a gate register. Weekday evenings after school and Sunday mornings are the slots families choose most. NXTutors lists home tutors who live in or near Survey Park first, then the Kasba & EM Bypass South zone and online tutors, and the first class is a free demo.

ajoy-nagar.name: Ajoy Nagar
ajoy-nagar.about:
Ajoy Nagar is a residential locality in the south-east of Kolkata, surrounded by Santoshpur, Mukundapur and Garia, with the EM Bypass close by. It falls in municipal ward 109 and shares its postcode with Survey Park. Homes are mainly flats in apartment buildings, many of them a few storeys high, with newer projects added as the bypass side has grown.

The Orange Line has served the area since March 2024. Jyotirindra Nandi station, at Mukundapur, and Satyajit Ray station, at Panchasayar, are the closest, and Kavi Subhash at New Garia, the line's southern end, is not far. Garia station on the Sealdah South main line gives tutors who travel by local train another way in, with autos and buses covering the last stretch.

In the smaller buildings a tutor walks straight up to the flat; newer complexes may ask for a name at the entrance. Families here usually choose a weekday slot after school or a Saturday morning. NXTutors lists home tutors who live in or around Ajoy Nagar first, then the rest of the Kasba & EM Bypass South zone and online tutors, and the first class with each tutor is a free demo.

birati.name: Birati
birati.about:
Birati is a neighbourhood in the North Dum Dum municipality of North 24 Parganas, next to the airport. Jessore Road runs along its east, the Kalyani Expressway along its west and the Belghoria Expressway to its south. The name is usually read as meaning a place to take a break. Birati has a long history: it was the seat of a local estate until 1716, and after 1757 it became part of the 24 Parganas granted to the East India Company.

Birati station on the Sealdah–Bangaon line is the local rail link, and Dum Dum Cantonment, further down the same line, connects with the Yellow Line metro, which has run to the airport since August 2025. A Yellow Line station under Jessore Road at Birati More is under construction. Homes are mainly in apartment buildings, with new projects still being added across the area.

Small apartment buildings mean the tutor usually goes straight to the door; larger complexes may want a name at the gate. Many tutors arrive by local train, so a lesson time that fits around the train timetable works well. NXTutors lists home tutors from Birati and the Lake Town, Dum Dum & Baguiati zone first, then online tutors, and the first class is a free demo.

kaikhali.name: Kaikhali
kaikhali.about:
Kaikhali is a neighbourhood of the Bidhannagar Municipal Corporation, in wards 5, 6 and 7, close to the airport at the northern end of VIP Road. Lake Town, Dum Dum Park, Kestopur, Baguiati, Nagerbazar, Teghoria, Chinar Park, New Town and Salt Lake are all nearby. VIP Road, completed in 1962, runs from Ultadanga past Lake Town, Kestopur, Baguiati and Teghoria to Kaikhali and the airport, and Kaikhali has been growing as both a residential and a commercial centre.

Homes are mostly flats in apartment buildings and gated enclaves along and behind VIP Road. A large number of bus routes run on VIP Road, and Jai Hind (Biman Bandar) and Jessore Road stations on the Yellow Line, open since August 2025, are the nearest metro. The Orange Line towards the airport is under construction.

Gated enclaves ask visitors to register, so share the tutor's name and flat number before the demo; smaller buildings are a doorstep visit. Tutors from Baguiati, Kestopur and Teghoria are close by, and families often pick a lesson time soon after school. NXTutors lists the nearest home tutors first, then the zone and online tutors, and the first class is a free demo.

hatibagan.name: Hatibagan
hatibagan.about:
Hatibagan is a well-known neighbourhood of North Kolkata, right next to Shyambazar, broadly covering municipal wards 10 and 11. Maniktala, Sovabazar and Bagbazar are close by. The name joins the Bengali words for elephant and garden; one story links it to elephants kept here during the attack on Calcutta in 1756. Hatibagan Market, one of the oldest traditional markets in the city, sells vegetables, fish, spices and more, and the area is also known for its many old theatres and cinema halls.

Shobhabazar Sutanuti and Shyambazar on the Blue Line are the nearest metro stations, and Kolkata station is the nearest railway terminal. Homes are mainly older family houses and apartment buildings on the lanes off the two main roads.

In an older house a tutor rings at the door and is let in directly; apartment buildings may ask for the tutor's name at the entrance. Because the market and the theatres keep the main roads lively into the evening, an after-school lesson that starts in the late afternoon is the usual choice. NXTutors lists home tutors from Hatibagan and the rest of North Kolkata first, then online tutors, and the first class is a free demo.

ultadanga.name: Ultadanga
ultadanga.about:
Ultadanga is a North Kolkata locality spread across municipal wards 13, 14 and 32, next to Maniktala and Beliaghata. It was one of the villages obtained by the East India Company in 1758 and became a fringe ward of the city in 1889. The name is said to come from Ulta Dingi, a place where small boats were made or repaired. Today it is densely built, with homes, government housing, apartment complexes, shops, offices and training institutes side by side.

Bidhannagar Road station, renamed from Ultadanga Road in 1972, sits on the Sealdah–Ranaghat line and the Circular Railway. Phoolbagan and Bengal Chemical stations on the Green Line, and Shyambazar and Shobhabazar Sutanuti on the Blue Line, are the nearest metro stops. VIP Road begins here, and CIT Road, the EM Bypass and Ultadanga Main Road meet at Hudco More, with the Ultadanga flyover, opened in 2011, rising over the crossing.

Government housing blocks and apartment complexes usually ask a visitor to sign in, so share the tutor's name in advance; older houses are a doorstep visit. Tutors from Salt Lake, Lake Town and north Kolkata can all reach Ultadanga easily, so families have a wide choice. NXTutors lists the nearest first, adds online tutors, and the first class is a free demo.

kankurgachi.name: Kankurgachi
kankurgachi.about:
Kankurgachi is a North Kolkata locality at the junction of Maniktala Main Road and CIT Road, with the EM Bypass along its eastern side, spread across municipal wards 30, 31 and 32. It was one of the villages known together as Dihi Panchannagram that the East India Company acquired in 1758, and its name comes from kankur, a kind of melon that grew well here. The Kankurgachi township began in the 1960s, at the same time as Salt Lake, and grew into a mixed community.

Housing today is largely high-rise apartment buildings, with older blocks from the township's early years. Three Green Line stations are within reach, Phoolbagan, Bengal Chemical and Salt Lake Stadium, and since August 2025 the line has run straight through from Howrah Maidan to Salt Lake Sector V, so tutors from Howrah, Sealdah and Salt Lake can all come by metro. CIT Road also carries many bus routes.

Most visits are to a flat in a building with a guard or intercom, so give the tutor's name and flat number in advance. An early-evening weekday lesson is the usual choice. NXTutors lists home tutors from Kankurgachi and the North Kolkata zone first, then online tutors, and the first class is a free demo.

phoolbagan.name: Phoolbagan
phoolbagan.about:
Phoolbagan is a North Kolkata locality at the junction of CIT Road and Narkeldanga Main Road, with the EM Bypass on its eastern edge. It covers parts of municipal wards 30, 31, 33 and 35, borders Beliaghata and Kankurgachi, and has its own police station on CIT Road. Both main roads were cut by the Calcutta Improvement Trust through older built-up areas in the 1930s. Subhas Sarovar, a large lake and one of the city's well-known open spaces, lies within the locality.

Homes are a mix of apartment buildings and independent houses on quiet residential streets. Phoolbagan station on the Green Line is right here, and since August 2025 the line has run through from Howrah to Salt Lake Sector V. Sealdah station, Sir Gurudas Banerjee Halt and Bidhannagar Road station are the nearby railway stops.

A house is a doorstep visit; apartment buildings may ask for a name at the entrance. With the metro station on the doorstep, tutors from Salt Lake, Sealdah and Howrah can all reach Phoolbagan, which gives families a wider choice. NXTutors lists home tutors nearest Phoolbagan first, then the North Kolkata zone and online tutors, and the first class is a free demo.

beliaghata.name: Beliaghata
beliaghata.about:
Beliaghata is a neighbourhood on the eastern side of central Kolkata, covering municipal wards 33 to 36. Maniktala, Ultadanga, Entally, Narkeldanga, Tangra and Phoolbagan are its neighbours. It was one of the villages, known together as Dihi Panchannagram, on which the East India Company obtained rights in 1717, and it was taken into the city's municipal area in 1889. Beleghata Sarkar Bari, a family house built in 1892, is a local heritage landmark.

The area is densely settled, and many homes are low houses along narrow lanes, with apartment buildings on the wider roads. Beliaghata Main Road leads to the EM Bypass, where Beleghata station on the Orange Line opened in August 2025, and CIT Road leads to Ultadanga. Phoolbagan on the Green Line and Sealdah, the nearest railway station, complete the links.

In the lanes a tutor often walks the last stretch from the main road and goes straight to the door; apartment buildings may ask for a name. Weekday evenings after school are the common slot. NXTutors lists home tutors from Beliaghata and the North Kolkata zone first, then online tutors, and the first class is a free demo.

baranagar.name: Baranagar
baranagar.about:
Baranagar is a town on the east bank of the Hooghly, just north of Kolkata, bounded by Dakshineswar to the north and South Dum Dum to the east. Its municipality, set up in 1869, is one of the oldest in India. The Dutch and Portuguese both had settlements here in the seventeenth century, and the first mechanised jute mill in India opened at Baranagar in 1859. Housing is mostly older apartment buildings and standalone houses.

Baranagar metro station, opened on 22 February 2021 as part of the Blue Line's extension to Dakshineswar, stands next to Baranagar Road station on the Sealdah–Dankuni suburban line. Barrackpore Trunk Road and the Belghoria Expressway pass through the town, and Dunlop crossing is one of the largest junctions on the northern edge of the city.

Standalone houses mean a doorstep visit; apartment buildings may want the tutor's name at the gate. With the metro and the suburban line side by side, tutors from north Kolkata and Dum Dum can reach Baranagar easily, and a lesson soon after school is the usual pick. NXTutors lists home tutors nearest Baranagar first, then online tutors, and the first class is a free demo.

liluah.name: Liluah
liluah.about:
Liluah is a neighbourhood on the northern side of Howrah, lying between Salkia and Belur. Its story is tied to the railway: the Carriage and Wagon Workshop moved here from near Howrah station around 1900 and became the largest combined carriage and wagon workshop of Indian Railways, and a railway colony for its staff had grown up by 1913. After independence the eastern side became mainly commercial and residential, while the western side kept some industry alongside new housing.

Liluah station is a major suburban stop, with platforms on both the Howrah–Bardhaman main line and the chord line, so tutors from across Howrah and the Hooghly side can arrive by local train. The Grand Trunk Road crosses the eastern part of Liluah and carries the buses. Hindi is widely spoken alongside Bengali, and many families look for a tutor comfortable in both.

Homes range from older railway-colony quarters to apartment buildings and houses; a house is a doorstep visit, while newer buildings may ask for a name. A slot timed around the local trains helps a tutor coming by rail. NXTutors lists home tutors from Liluah and the Howrah zone first, then online tutors, and the first class with each is a free demo.

bally.name: Bally
bally.about:
Bally is the northernmost part of Howrah, on the west bank of the Hooghly. Bally Canal separates it from Uttarpara in Hooghly district, and a bridge was built over the canal in 1846 to join the two. Belur and Liluah lie to its south. Two road and rail bridges, Vivekananda Setu and Nivedita Setu, cross the river to Dakshineswar, and the Grand Trunk Road and the Belghoria Expressway pass through. Housing is a mix of apartment buildings and family houses.

Bally has three stations on the suburban network, Bally, Bally Ghat and Bally Halt, and Dakshineswar, the northern end of the Blue Line, is just across the river. That gives tutors from north Kolkata and Baranagar a direct way over the bridges, as well as tutors from Howrah and the Hooghly towns by local train.

A family house is a doorstep visit, while newer apartment buildings may ask for a name at the gate. A weekday after-school slot is the usual choice, timed to suit a tutor arriving by train. NXTutors lists home tutors from Bally and the Howrah zone first, then the wider city and online tutors, and the first class with each is a free demo.

kadamtala.name: Kadamtala
kadamtala.about:
Kadamtala is a neighbourhood in central Howrah, spread across Howrah Municipal Corporation wards 21 to 24 and 43, and served by Bantra police station. It grew with the railway: after Howrah terminus opened in 1854, flour mills followed in 1855, then jute mills, and after the Second World War the area turned to small iron-casting works. Today Kadamtala is mainly residential, though many small workshops remain. New HIT Road and the Drainage Canal Road are among its main roads.

Dasnagar and Tikiapara on the South Eastern suburban line are the nearest stations, and Howrah station, one of the country's busiest, is close by. Howrah Maidan station, the western terminus of the Green Line, opened in March 2024 on the Grand Trunk Road, and since August 2025 the line has run straight through under the river to Sealdah and Salt Lake Sector V.

Homes here are mostly houses and apartment buildings of a few storeys, so a tutor usually goes straight to the door. That metro link means a tutor from Kolkata can now reach Kadamtala as easily as one from elsewhere in Howrah. NXTutors lists home tutors from Kadamtala and the Howrah zone first, then online tutors, and the first class is a free demo.
